title: "Rental Market Analysis"
author: "Giuliana Vazquez"
date: "2026-04-01"
output: html_document
---

```{r}
rm(list = ls())

if (!require("ipumsr")) install.packages("ipumsr")
library(ipumsr)
if (!require("dplyr")) install.packages("dplyr")
library(dplyr)
if (!require("stargazer")) install.packages("stargazer")
library(stargazer)
if (!require("fixest")) install.packages("fixest")
library(fixest)
if (!require("modelsummary")) install.packages("modelsummary")
library(modelsummary)
if (!require("ggplot2")) install.packages("ggplot2")
library(ggplot2)

setwd('/Users/Giul/Desktop/econ project')
ddi <- read_ipums_ddi("usa_00004.xml")
data <- read_ipums_micro(ddi)

dim(data)
names(data)

#each household is now represented by the same reference person (head of household)
hh <- data %>%
  filter(PERNUM == 1)
cat("Household reference-person rows:", nrow(hh), "\n")

#take out werid values
#change to log rent and log income 1 = employed and 0 = unemployed
#id for fixed effects
#fixed employment to be 
hh_rent <- hh %>%
  filter(RENTGRS > 0, RENTGRS < 99999) %>%
  mutate(
    ln_rent = log(RENTGRS),
    puma_id = paste0(STATEFIP, "_", PUMA),
    employed = ifelse(EMPSTAT == 1, 1, 0),
    ln_income = ifelse(HHINCOME > 0, log(HHINCOME), NA_real_),
    income_10k = HHINCOME / 10000
  )
cat("Renter households with valid rent:", nrow(hh_rent), "\n")


#Chicago, NYC, SF
hh_rent <- hh_rent %>%
  mutate(
    city = case_when(
      STATEFIP == 17 & COUNTYFIP == 31 ~ "Chicago",
      STATEFIP == 36 & COUNTYFIP %in% c(5, 47, 61, 81, 85) ~ "NYC",
      STATEFIP == 6  & COUNTYFIP == 75 ~ "San Francisco",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

#keep whats need drop the rest
hh_cities <- hh_rent %>%
  filter(!is.na(city))

table(hh_cities$city)

hh_final <- hh_cities %>%
  filter(
    HHINCOME > 0,
    !is.na(EDUC),
    !is.na(AGE),
    !is.na(SEX),
    !is.na(employed),
    !is.na(BEDROOMS),
    !is.na(UNITSSTR)
  )
cat("Final analysis sample:", nrow(hh_final), "\n")

#dummy variables
hh_final <- hh_final %>%
  mutate(
    female = ifelse(SEX == 2, 1, 0),
    high_school = ifelse(EDUC >= 6, 1, 0),
    college = ifelse(EDUC >= 10, 1, 0)
  )

  
#clean data set for submission
cleandataset <- hh_final
write.csv(cleandataset, "cleaneddataset.csv", row.names = FALSE)

#summary table
datasummary(
  ln_rent + RENTGRS + income_10k + ln_income + high_school + college + employed + AGE + female + BEDROOMS + UNITSSTR ~ 
    Mean + SD + Min + Median + Max + N,
  data = hh_final,
)


#Regression models

#model 1: baseline
model1 <- feols(
  ln_rent ~ income_10k + high_school + college + employed,
  data = hh_final,
  cluster = ~puma_id
)
summary(model1)

#model 2: baseline w/ demographic controls
model2 <- feols(
  ln_rent ~ income_10k + high_school + college + employed + AGE + female,
  data = hh_final,
  cluster = ~puma_id
)
summary(model2)

#model 3: model 2 + fixed effects
model3 <- feols(
  ln_rent ~ income_10k + high_school + college + employed + AGE + female | YEAR + puma_id,
  data = hh_final,
  cluster = ~puma_id
)
summary(model3)

#model 4: robustness check - log income to see if my results are sensitive to how i measure income?
model4 <- feols(
  ln_rent ~ ln_income + high_school + college + employed + AGE + female | YEAR + puma_id,
  data = hh_final %>% filter(!is.na(ln_income)),
  cluster = ~puma_id
)
summary(model4)

#model 5: preferred model 
# Add housing controls
model5 <- feols(
  ln_rent ~ income_10k + high_school + college + employed + AGE + female + BEDROOMS + UNITSSTR | YEAR + puma_id,
  data = hh_final,
  cluster = ~puma_id
)
summary(model5)

#model 6: robustness check - remove extreme incomes to answer the question: are my results being driven by really rich outliers??
hh_trim <- hh_final %>%
  filter(HHINCOME > 0 & HHINCOME < 300000)

model6 <- feols(
  ln_rent ~ income_10k + high_school + college + employed + AGE + female + BEDROOMS + UNITSSTR | YEAR + puma_id,
  data = hh_trim,
  cluster = ~puma_id
)
summary(model6)

modelsummary(
  list(
    "(1)" = model1,
    "(2)" = model2,
    "(3)" = model3,
    "(4)" = model4,
    "(5)" = model5,
    "(6)" = model6
  ),
  stars = TRUE,
  gof_omit = "IC|Log|Adj|RMSE",
)

etable(model1, model2, model3, model4, model5, model6)


#city comparison
modelchicago <- feols(
  ln_rent ~ income_10k + high_school + college + employed + AGE + female + BEDROOMS + UNITSSTR | YEAR + puma_id,
  data = hh_final %>% filter(city == "Chicago"),
  cluster = ~puma_id
)

modelnyc <- feols(
  ln_rent ~ income_10k + high_school + college + employed + AGE + female + BEDROOMS + UNITSSTR | YEAR + puma_id,
  data = hh_final %>% filter(city == "NYC"),
  cluster = ~puma_id
)

modelsf <- feols(
  ln_rent ~ income_10k + high_school + college + employed + AGE + female + BEDROOMS + UNITSSTR | YEAR + puma_id,
  data = hh_final %>% filter(city == "San Francisco"),
  cluster = ~puma_id
)

modelsummary(
  list(
    "Chicago" = modelchicago,
    "New York City" = modelnyc,
    "San Francisco" = modelsf
  ),
  stars = TRUE,
  gof_omit = "IC|Log|Adj|RMSE",
)

etable(modelchicago, modelnyc, modelsf)

#graph
citycollegesummary <- hh_final %>%
  mutate(college_label = ifelse(college == 1, "College Degree", "No College Degree")) %>%
  group_by(city, college_label) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_rent = mean(RENTGRS, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(citycollegesummary)

ggplot(citycollegesummary, aes(x = city, y = avg_rent, fill = college_label)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "Average Monthly Gross Rent by City and College Status",
    x = "City",
    y = "Average Monthly Gross Rent ($)",
    fill = "Education"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
